title: 实验 5-12 · LM1117 稳压器与压差：为什么锂电池 + AMS1117 不行
summary: 稳压电源 → LM1117-3.3（输入、输出各 10 µF）→ ESP32 的 3V3 脚（拔掉 USB）。把输入从 5 V 往下调到锂电池的电压，看稳压区、压差区和欠压复位，再算稳压器的发热。
concepts: 线性稳压器 linear regulator / LDO
description: **目标**：用 LM1117-3.3 线性稳压器给 ESP32 供电，改变输入电压，看稳压区、压差（dropout）区和欠压复位，并算出稳压器的发热。
- 稳压电源 PS1（5 V）的 + 接 U2（LM1117-3.3，正面朝你 GND OUT IN）的 **IN**，− 接 GND。
- C1（10 µF）从 IN 到 GND，C2（10 µF）从 OUT 到 GND，都尽量靠近稳压器。
- U2 的 OUT 接 ESP32 的 **3V3** 脚，ESP32 的 GND 接 GND。ESP32 **拔掉 USB**（属性里 usb 关掉），完全由这个稳压器供电。
- 负载指示：任意输出 GPIO（参考答案 GPIO4，设为输出高）→ R1（330 Ω）→ 红色 LED → GND。芯片在运行时 LED 亮。
**引脚设置**：参考答案把 GPIO4 设为输出高；测试也会设一次。ESP32 的 **usb: false** 是题目要求。
**线性稳压器的原理**：它就是一个自动调节的“可变电阻”，串在输入和输出之间，把多余的电压吃掉。所以：
- 输出永远比输入低——至少低一个**压差**。LM1117 的输入至少要比输出高约 **1.1 V**。
- 输入电流 ≈ 输出电流（+ 静态电流），效率 ≈ Vout/Vin。
- 发热 **P = (Vin − Vout) × I**。
**先预测**：负载约 56 mA（ESP32 芯片约 50 mA + LED 4 mA），稳压器的压差模型是“输出 = 输入 − 1.1 V − 0.2 Ω × I”，ESP32 的欠压阈值（仿真）是 2.5 V。电源为 5 V、4.0 V、3.7 V、3.4 V、9 V 时，OUT 各是多少？哪一档 ESP32 会复位、LED 会灭？5 V 和 9 V 时稳压器各发热多少瓦，效率各是多少？
**测量**：测试会把电源电压依次设成 5 V、4.0 V、3.7 V、3.4 V、9 V，看输出电压和 LED。电路检查通过后，把读数填进下面的「测量」（以你自己的面包板为准）；答完后会显示计算对比。
**实际项目经验**：
- **锂电池（3.0–4.2 V）+ AMS1117-3.3 是经典错误**：满电 4.2 V 时勉强够，电池电压一降到 4.0 V 以下，3.3 V 就开始往下掉，ESP32 一开 Wi-Fi 就复位。要选真正的低压差 LDO：**ME6211、HT7333、XC6220、RT9080**（压差 0.1–0.25 V），或者 Buck-Boost 开关电源。
- ESP32-DevKitC 板上就是 AMS1117，所以用锂电池时不要接到 5V 脚，而是用低压差 LDO 接到 3V3 脚。
- LDO 的**输出电容**不能省：LM1117 / AMS1117 要 ≥ 10 µF（钽电容或数据手册允许的 ESR），否则可能自激振荡；输入电容让它在电源线很长时也稳定。ESP32 旁边再加 100 µF 吸收 Wi-Fi 的电流尖峰。
- 电流大、压差大时用开关电源（Buck）：12 V → 3.3 V、500 mA 用 LDO 要发热 4.4 W，根本不现实。
- 3V3 脚外部供电时**不要同时插 USB**（两个电源打架），也不要超过 3.6 V。
**模型说明**：LDO 模型：稳压 / 压差（输出 = 输入 − 1.1 V − 0.2 Ω × I）/ 限流 800 mA / 关断，静态电流 5 mA。ESP32 的负载按约 50 mA 建模，没有 Wi-Fi 的电流尖峰；欠压阈值取 2.5 V（真实芯片的欠压检测约 2.4–2.8 V，而且官方要求 3.0–3.6 V 才保证正常工作）。电容在直流下不起作用，这里只是检查有没有接。

en.title: Experiment 5-12 · LM1117 regulator and dropout: why a Li-ion cell + AMS1117 fails
en.summary: Bench supply → LM1117-3.3 (10 µF in and out) → the ESP32's 3V3 pin (USB unplugged). Turn the input down from 5 V to Li-ion voltages to see regulation, dropout and brown-out reset, and work out the regulator's heat.
description: **Goal**: power an ESP32 from an LM1117-3.3 linear regulator, vary the input voltage, and see regulation, dropout and brown-out reset; work out the regulator's heat.
**Circuit**:
- Bench supply PS1 (5 V): + to the **IN** pin of U2 (LM1117-3.3, printed face towards you: GND OUT IN), − to GND.
- C1 (10 µF) from IN to GND and C2 (10 µF) from OUT to GND, both close to the regulator.
- U2's OUT to the ESP32's **3V3** pin, the ESP32's GND to GND. **Unplug the ESP32's USB** (turn usb off in Properties) so it runs only from this regulator.
- Load indicator: any output GPIO (the reference uses GPIO4, output HIGH) → R1 (330 Ω) → red LED → GND. The LED is lit while the chip runs.
**Pin table settings**: the reference sets GPIO4 to output HIGH (the tests set it too). The ESP32's **usb: false** is part of the task.
**How a linear regulator works**: it is a self-adjusting "variable resistor" in series between input and output that eats the extra voltage. So:
- The output is always lower than the input — by at least the **dropout**. The LM1117 needs its input at least about **1.1 V** above its output.
- Input current ≈ output current (+ quiescent current), efficiency ≈ Vout/Vin.
- Heat **P = (Vin − Vout) × I**.

**Predict first**: the load is about 56 mA (about 50 mA for the ESP32 chip + 4 mA LED), the dropout model is "out = in − 1.1 V − 0.2 Ω × I", and the simulated ESP32 browns out at 2.5 V. What is OUT with the supply at 5 V, 4.0 V, 3.7 V, 3.4 V and 9 V? At which setting does the ESP32 reset and the LED go off? How many watts does the regulator dissipate at 5 V and at 9 V, and what is the efficiency?

**Measure**: the tests set the supply to 5 V, 4.0 V, 3.7 V, 3.4 V and 9 V in turn and check the output voltage and the LED. Once the circuit check passes, type your readings into the Measurements below (whatever your own board shows); the worked comparison appears after you answer.
**Rule of thumb for real projects**:

- **Li-ion (3.0–4.2 V) + AMS1117-3.3 is the classic mistake**: it scrapes by at a full 4.2 V, but below about 4.0 V the 3.3 V rail sags and the ESP32 resets as soon as Wi-Fi transmits. Use a real low-dropout part — **ME6211, HT7333, XC6220, RT9080** (0.1–0.25 V dropout) — or a buck-boost converter.
- The ESP32-DevKitC itself carries an AMS1117, so on a Li-ion cell don't feed the 5V pin: use a low-dropout LDO into the 3V3 pin.

- Don't skip the LDO's **output capacitor**: the LM1117 / AMS1117 needs ≥ 10 µF (tantalum, or the ESR the datasheet allows) or it may oscillate; the input capacitor keeps it stable with long supply leads. Add 100 µF near the ESP32 for the Wi-Fi current bursts.
- For high current and a big voltage difference use a switching (buck) regulator: 12 V → 3.3 V at 500 mA would burn 4.4 W in an LDO — not realistic.
- When feeding the 3V3 pin from outside, **don't plug USB in at the same time** (two supplies fighting), and never exceed 3.6 V.

**Model note**: the LDO model has regulate / dropout (out = in − 1.1 V − 0.2 Ω × I) / current limit 800 mA / off, with 5 mA quiescent current. The ESP32 load is about 50 mA without Wi-Fi bursts; brown-out is at 2.5 V (a real chip's brown-out detector sits around 2.4–2.8 V, and Espressif only guarantees operation at 3.0–3.6 V). Capacitors do nothing at DC; here they are only checked for being present.
compare: - **5 V**: regulating, OUT = **3.30 V**; load ≈ **56 mA**, the supply gives 61 mA (the extra 5 mA is the regulator's own quiescent current). Dissipation P = (5.0 − 3.3) × 0.056 ≈ **0.12 W**, efficiency 66 %.
- **4.0 V**: in **dropout**, OUT = 4.0 − 1.1 − 0.2 Ω × I ≈ **2.89 V**; the ESP32 still runs and the LED dims.
- **3.7 V** (a Li-ion cell's nominal voltage): OUT ≈ **2.59 V**, just above the brown-out threshold. A GPIO "HIGH" is now only about 2.6 V.
- **3.4 V** (an almost empty Li-ion cell): OUT ≈ **2.29 V**, the ESP32 **browns out**, every pin goes high-impedance and the LED goes off.
- **9 V**: still 3.30 V, but the regulator turns (9 − 3.3) × 0.056 ≈ **0.36 W** into heat; efficiency only 37 %.
- With Wi-Fi on, an ESP32 peaks at 300–500 mA: from 5 V that is 0.5–0.85 W, already very hot for a small SOT-223.

measurements.ask: Supply at 4.0 V: the regulator's OUT to GND
measurements.explain: Dropout: OUT ≈ 4.0 − 1.1 − 0.2 Ω × I ≈ 2.89 V, no longer 3.3 V.

measurements.ask: Supply at 9 V: the drop across the regulator U_IN − U_OUT (red lead on IN, black on OUT)
Supply at 9 V: the regulator's output current (put the ammeter in series in the OUT → ESP32 3V3 wire)
Heat in the regulator at 9 V, P = (U_IN − U_OUT) × I (from your readings)
measurements.explain: A linear regulator turns all the extra voltage into heat: (9 − 3.3) V × 56 mA ≈ 0.32 W, an efficiency of only 3.3/9 ≈ 37%.

hints: LM1117 legs with the printed face towards you: GND, OUT, IN. The supply goes to IN (right leg).
10 µF from IN to GND and 10 µF from OUT to GND; OUT to the ESP32's 3V3 pin.
Select the ESP32 and switch usb off — otherwise USB powers it and the experiment shows nothing.
tests: 4.0 V in: dropout, ESP32 still running
3.7 V in (Li-ion): a GPIO HIGH drops too
3.4 V in: ESP32 browns out, LED off
9 V in: still regulating, but the regulator heats up

tests.name: 输入 4.0 V：压差区，ESP32 还在运行
输入 3.7 V（锂电池）：GPIO 的高电平也跟着降低
输入 3.4 V：ESP32 欠压复位，LED 灭
输入 9 V：仍然稳压，但稳压器发热

compare: - **3.7 V**（锂电池的标称电压）：OUT ≈ **2.59 V**，ESP32 刚刚高于欠压阈值。GPIO 的“高电平”也只有 2.6 V 左右。
- **3.4 V**（锂电池快没电）：OUT ≈ **2.29 V**，ESP32 **欠压复位**，所有引脚变高阻，LED 灭。
- ESP32 开 Wi-Fi 时峰值电流 300–500 mA：从 5 V 降压要发热 0.5–0.85 W，SOT-223 小封装已经很烫。

measurements.ask: 电源调到 4.0 V：稳压器 OUT 对 GND 的电压
measurements.explain: 进入压差区：OUT ≈ 4.0 − 1.1 − 0.2 Ω × I ≈ 2.89 V，已经不是 3.3 V。

measurements.ask: 电源调到 9 V：稳压器上的压降 U_IN − U_OUT（红表笔 IN，黑表笔 OUT）
电源调到 9 V：稳压器的输出电流（把电流表串进 OUT 到 ESP32 3V3 的连线里读）
9 V 时稳压器的发热 P = (U_IN − U_OUT) × I（用你的读数算）
measurements.explain: 线性稳压器把多余的电压全变成热：(9 − 3.3) V × 56 mA ≈ 0.32 W，效率只有 3.3/9 ≈ 37%。

hints: LM1117 正面朝你，三只脚是 GND、OUT、IN。电源接 IN（右脚）。
IN 到 GND 一个 10 µF，OUT 到 GND 一个 10 µF；OUT 接 ESP32 的 3V3 脚。
选中 ESP32，把 usb 关掉——否则它从 USB 取电，实验就看不出效果。
